question: A ball is thrown upward with an initial velocity of 12 m/s. What will be its velocity after 1 second? (Take g = 9.8 m/s²)
solution:
The correct answer is __**2.2 m/s**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The motion of the ball follows the **first equation of motion**, which relates final velocity, initial velocity, acceleration, and time.
 
• Given data: The **initial velocity (u)** is **12 m/s**, the **time (t)** is **1 second**, and the **acceleration due to gravity (g)** is **9.8 m/s²**.
 
• When an object is thrown **upward**, it moves against the force of gravity. Therefore, the **acceleration (a)** is taken as **-g**, which is **-9.8 m/s²**. ***Hence, statement 1 is correct in its application of sign convention.***
 
• Applying the formula **v = u + at**, we substitute the values: **v = 12 + (-9.8 × 1)**.
 
• The calculation results in **v = 12 - 9.8**, which equals **2.2 m/s**. ***Hence, the final velocity after 1 second is 2.2 m/s.***
 
• Since the resulting **velocity** is positive, it indicates that the ball is **still moving upward** but at a significantly reduced speed due to the constant downward pull of **gravity**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Equations of Motion:**

 
 
• These equations describe the behavior of a physical system in terms of its motion as a function of **time**. They are valid only when **acceleration is constant**.
 
• **First Equation:** **v = u + at** (Velocity-Time relation).
 
• **Second Equation:** **s = ut + 1/2 at²** (Position-Time relation), where **s** is **displacement**.
 
• **Third Equation:** **v² = u² + 2as** (Velocity-Position relation).
 
 
 
• **Acceleration due to Gravity (g):**
 
 
• On **Earth**, the standard value for **g** is approximately **9.8 m/s²**. It represents the constant acceleration experienced by an object in **free fall**.
 
• The value of **g** varies slightly depending on the **location** (altitude and latitude), being higher at the **poles** and lower at the **equator**.
 
 
 
• **Sign Convention in Kinematics:**
 
 
• In vertical motion, if we consider the **upward direction** as positive, then **initial velocity (u)** is positive, and **acceleration due to gravity (g)** is negative because it acts **downward**.
 
• At the **maximum height** of the trajectory, the **final velocity (v)** of the object becomes **0 m/s** momentarily before it starts descending.
 
 
 
• **Scalar vs Vector Quantities:**
 
 
• **Velocity** is a **vector quantity**, meaning it has both **magnitude** and **direction**. In this problem, the magnitude is **2.2 m/s** and the direction is **upward**.
 
• **Speed** is a **scalar quantity** and only represents the magnitude of the rate of motion.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• If the **time** given was longer, such as **2 seconds**, the velocity would become **negative** (12 - 19.6 = -7.6 m/s), indicating the ball has already reached its peak and is **falling back down**.
 
• The **maximum height** reached by the ball can be calculated using the formula **s = u² / 2g**. For an initial velocity of **12 m/s**, the maximum height would be approximately **7.35 meters**.
 
• The **total time of flight** for the ball to return to the thrower's hand (ignoring air resistance) is calculated as **T = 2u / g**, which would be approximately **2.45 seconds**.
